newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES USE FOUR HOMERS TO BEAT ORIOLES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES USE FOUR HOMERS TO BEAT ORIOLES.

text.p: The New York Yankees beat the Baltimore Orioles at their own game on Saturday, using the long ball to score an 8-4 victory and move within one win of the World Series.
Darryl Strawberry homered twice and Bernie Williams and Paul O'Neill also homered to give the Yankees a commanding 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven American League Championship Series.

"Tonight was a big night for me. I went out and did a good job. I'm just happy about it," said Strawberry, the troubled slugger whose career was rescued from oblivion when the Yankees signed him this season.
The New York bullpen worked its magic once again as four Yankee relievers combined for six scoreless innings after starter Kenny Rogers left in the fourth.
Reliever David Weathers got the victory. He allowed three hits over 2 2/3 innings as the Yankees won for the first time without trailing in eight post-season games.
"The big reason we beat them is the pitching," said Yankees manager Joe Torre. "The bullpen is carrying the torch for us."
The Orioles broke the 1961 Yankees' record for most home runs in a season this year, but they managed just one solo shot from Chris Hoiles in the third inning Saturday.
New York, in contrast, took rookie starter Rocky Coppinger long three times in the first four innings.

"I made three bad pitches today and every one of them left the park. I don't know if that's because of inexperience or not," said Coppinger, who was tagged for five runs and six hits over 5 1/3 innings in his playoff debut.
Williams continued to wield a big bat for the Yanks. He launched his fifth post-season homer -- a two-run blast in the first inning -- to stake New York to a 2-0 lead.
The Orioles answered with a run in the bottom of the first on Rafael Palmeiro's sacrifice fly.
Strawberry led off the second by belting an 0-1 pitch over the right-field scoreboard to give the Yankees a 3-1 edge.
After Hoiles brought the Orioles back to within 3-2, Strawberry singled in the fourth and O'Neill drilled a 2-1 pitch into the bleachers in left-centre to make it 5-2.
Baltimore scratched out two more runs to the bottom of the inning on a B.J. Surhoff RBI single and an RBI groundout by Hoiles to make it a a one-run ballgame once again.
The score remained 5-4 until the critical eighth inning.
In the top of the eighth, Cecil Fielder delivered an RBI groundout to give the Yankees a two-run cushion.
Strawberry then smacked his second homer of the night, a two-out, two-run shot off Armando Benitez that made it 8-4.
"It's electric to hit a home run in this atmosphere," said Strawberry, a member of the world champion New York Mets in 1986. "Post-season play is what it's all about."
The Orioles tagged New York reliever Mariano Rivera for three straight singles to load the bases with none out in the bottom of the eighth. But Baltimore failed to score a run.

Rivera struck out Hoiles and Brady Anderson, who had 50 home runs during the regular season, and then got Todd Zeile to pop out, ending the threat. John Wetteland pitched a perfect ninth to seal the win.
"We loaded up the bases against Rivera and he turned the valve up a notch," said Baltimore manager Davey Johnson.
In all, Baltimore left 10 men stranded on base as New York raised its record to 8-0 this year at Camden Yards with their second successive post-season win here.
"It's a tough question and there's no good explanation why they are always able to beat us," said Johnson.
"It's probably their pitching, especially their bullpen. We have guys who have gone a little bit cold at the wrong time."
The Yankees need only win one of the next three games to reach the World Series for the first time in 15 years. Baltimore must sweep the last three to move on.
"I think we might play a little looser, believe it or not, tomorrow," said Zeile. "No one really expects us to win. It's still a possibility, it could come down to Game 7."
But first they must win Game 5 Sunday in Baltimore, where the Yankees feel right at home.
"We played well here all year," said O'Neil. "Straw had a huge game. Bernie (Williams) and (Derek) Jeter did a great job. It was a good team win."
